title: Eval Monoculture + Model Homogeneity: Correlated Blind Spots at Scale

original_idea.title: Eval Monoculture + Model Homogeneity: Correlated Blind Spots at Scale
original_idea.problem: If all major models share architectural similarities AND are all evaluated on the same narrow benchmark set, the blind spots are correlated: behaviors that the benchmark doesn't cover AND that the architecture is prone to fail on will escape undetected across all deployed models simultaneously.
original_idea.direction: Empirically test for correlated blind spots: identify safety behaviors not covered by the top 5 widely-used benchmarks, test whether architecturally similar open-source models fail on these behaviors at correlated rates. Measure whether architectural diversity reduces correlation.
original_idea.why_it_matters: Correlated failures across all deployed models are a systemic risk orders of magnitude worse than uncorrelated individual model failures.
original_idea.relevant_context: The 2025 FLI Safety Index notes 'shared blind spots undermine benchmarks.' Stanford's benchmark bugs research found bugs causing systematic multi-model failures.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: demonstrating correlated blind spots would motivate both benchmark diversification and architectural diversity in deployed systems. Every link from measurement to policy motivation is explicit.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Running existing benchmarks on open-source models is intermediate-level. Identifying uncovered safety behaviors and measuring correlation requires some statistical knowledge but standard tools suffice.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Requires identifying uncovered behaviors, testing multiple models, and computing correlations. A focused version testing 2-3 models on one specific gap category could fit 30 hours with sustained effort.

novelty.reasoning: Correlated errors in LLMs have been empirically demonstrated (arxiv 2506.07962: 350+ LLMs show 60% error correlation on leaderboard datasets, with larger models showing higher correlation). The 'Safetywashing' paper (arxiv 2407.21792) shows safety benchmarks correlate with general capabilities. The specific framing of correlated blind spots across architecturally similar models on safety-specific behaviors is partially addressed -- the correlated errors paper covers general benchmarks but the safety-specific angle with architectural diversity measurement adds some novelty.
